THE DROWNED APPROACH. Eight slots, and this table was RETUNED TWICE after it
was measured, because the first cut of it was quietly the hardest patch of
wild Kin in the game.

WHERE IT FIRES, AND WHY THAT IS THE DESIGN. The engine rolls an encounter on
any tile whose terrain declares one, and on this map exactly one character
does: W. Aurelian floor does not, shallow water does not, the quay does not.
So the player decides their own exposure by deciding whether to be in the
water -- the landing hall, the quay lip, the dais in the middle of the nave
and all four rock pockets are safe ground, and the swim between them is not.
That matters more here than on any route in the game, because the hardest
battle in the story is two floors north of this room, and a player who arrives
at it worn down has been robbed by a corridor rather than beaten by a
commander.

RATE 80 RATHER THAN THE USUAL 150, FOR THE SAME REASON. The nave is about
twenty rows of open water and the pockets are a detour off it; at the standard
rate a player going for all four rewards fights nine or ten times to get them,
which turns the payoff of a brand new field art into a toll. Eighty makes the
crossing roughly a coin flip and the full circuit about four fights.

MEASURED, AND THE FIRST CUT FAILED. tests/helpers/simulate.mjs, novice tier,
lone lead, 400 runs per row, worst case in brackets is the top of every band.

  first cut: six Kin, every one of them Tide-typed, at levels 41-45
    L45   flame 45% [39%]   verdant 94% [87%]   tide 74% [67%]
  route_10, the last road before the eighth Hall, for the same player
    L45   flame 86%         verdant  94%        tide 84%

A Flame player would have arrived at the climax having lost one wild fight in
two on the way in, on a map whose entire job is to hand them a new field art
and let them enjoy using it -- and the player has asked four times for an
easier game. Half the reference is not a difficulty choice, it is a bug with
a plausible excuse.

TWO THINGS FIXED IT. The band came down to 38-42, at or just under route_10s,
because this is where the player arrives rather than somewhere they grind to.
And the Tide monoculture was broken, which was the real fault: every Kin in
the first cut carried Tide, Tide is 2x into Flame, and no amount of reweighting
six Tide Kin against each other changes what all six of them hit a Flame lead
with. tidewrack -- which resists Flame four ways to one and was the HEAVIEST
slot at twenty per cent -- is down to five, and two Kin a Flame lead can
actually hit went in at twenty and fourteen.

  silthopper  terra/chitin, a tidal-flats native, and a thing that crosses open
              mud without walking belongs on a drowned floor.
  lantric     spark/iron, and it does not live in the sea at all. It is here
              for a reason written on the wall of the east arm: there is a new
              armoured sixty-conductor trunk running through this ruin carrying
              more current than Aureline draws on a winter night, and lantric is
              the Kin that hangs itself on things and burns steady for eleven
              hours. It is the only encounter slot in this game placed by an
              electrical fault.

AFTER, same method:
    L44   flame 70% [61%]   verdant 96% [90%]   tide 93% [85%]
    L45   flame 74% [66%]   verdant 97% [95%]   tide 95% [89%]
    L46   flame 75% [69%]   verdant 98% [97%]   tide 95% [91%]

Flame still sits about twelve points under the reference road and that is left
alone deliberately: this is the ocean act, Tide is 2x into Flame, and a type
chart that stops applying at the climax is not a type chart. Twelve points off
is the chart working. Half is the table being badly built.

EIGHT SLOTS, SEVEN TYPE PAIRS, and no two of the top four sharing a weakness.
maelstrix is the rare one at five per cent and the only fully evolved head of a
line down here; meeting one should be an event.
